definition: Systems that detect or forecast an imminent hazard and decide and issue warnings (multi-hazard early warning systems, threshold-based alerting, warning centres). Does not include the channels that carry the warning, sector-specific warnings of disease, pests or pollution, or alerting standards.
Location-based public alerts sent through mobile networks by cell broadcast. Does not include SMS or other channels.

type_name: Other public warning channels and last-mile reach
definition: Carrying warnings to the exposed public by SMS, applications, sirens, radio, television or community networks, including reaching remote or last-mile populations. Does not include cell broadcast, warnings to institutions or responders, or the systems that issue warnings.
Warning specific institutions, staff, schools, responders or road users so that they trigger contingency or protective action. Does not include warnings to the general public.

Early warning for a sector-specific hazard: climate-sensitive disease outbreaks, crop pests, or water pollution, linking surveillance or monitoring to warnings. Does not include multi-hazard warnings of floods, storms or droughts.

Adopting common alerting standards (such as the Common Alerting Protocol) or linking alert systems across agencies so warnings are coordinated. Does not include building the systems or channels themselves.
Provides warning capabilities covering multiple hazards
Generates, manages or disseminates official alerts
Extends warnings to exposed populations or locations
An emergency call-taking, dispatch or case-handling platform or centre (a 911 or 112 service and its operators, caller geolocation and call routing).
Sending warnings and alerts to the public or to communities at risk: SMS, cell broadcast, sirens, radio and television, mobile applications, last-mile dissemination.
Hydrological, meteorological, seismic or health surveillance networks, sensors, data and forecasting systems that detect a hazard and generate the warning.
Standard operating procedures, protocols, standards, agreements and agency coordination for issuing warnings and responding to them.
Emergency operations centres, dedicated emergency radio or data networks, and the connectivity and facilities that let warnings and responders communicate.
Training of operators and responders, and awareness campaigns so people know the service or the warnings and how to act on them.
